newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Buenos Aires mayor challenges Menem on poll date.
newsitem.headline: Buenos Aires mayor challenges Menem on poll date.

text.p: Fernando de la Rua, the mayor of Argentina's capital, challenged Friday President Carlos Menem's power to set the date of Congressional elections in the city.
"We are sending an appeal to the (Supreme) Court as soon as possible to resolve the conflict of the date of the elections," de la Rua said in a statement published by private news agency DyN.
The mayor argues constitutional changes give him the right to decide the date of Buenos Aires elections.
Menem signed a decree Wednesday setting mid-term Congressional elections in Buenos Aires for October 26, the same day as the rest of the country.
Menem is trying "to take back this power because he expects bad results" in the Buenos Aires vote, said de la Rua who wants the city to hold elections on June 29.

De la Rua, of the opposition Radical Party, was elected in the first vote ever in the capital for the post of mayor last year after a constitutional change in 1994. Before that the mayor of the capital had been appointed by the president.
De la Rua is one of the front-runners in the 1999 presidential elections. Menem cannot stand for a third term because the constitution prevents him from doing so.
